question.stem: An earthquake produces P waves, which are longitudinal, and S waves, which are transverse. Both travel through the Earth's crust to a seismic station. In the crust, P waves travel at 6.0 $\text{km s}^{-1}$ and S waves at 3.5 $\text{km s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Outline the difference between the motion of particles of the crust when a P wave passes and when an S wave passes.
markscheme: P wave: particles oscillate parallel to the direction in which the wave travels (energy is transferred) ✓
S wave: particles oscillate perpendicular to the direction in which the wave travels ✓

parts.label: b
parts.question: The S wave arrives at the station 42 s after the P wave. Show that the station is about 350 km from the earthquake.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: The graph shows how the vertical displacement of the ground at the station varies with time as the S wave passes. Determine, in km, the wavelength of the S wave.
markscheme: period read from the graph: $T = 1.25$ s (or $f = 1/T$) ✓

mistakes.feedback: Wavelength = speed × period (or speed ÷ frequency), not speed ÷ period.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: State the total distance moved by a particle of the ground at the station during one period of the S wave.

mistakes.feedback: In one period the particle goes up and down and back again: four times the amplitude.

vp.what: speed of P waves in the crust

vs.what: speed of S waves in the crust

dt.what: time between the arrival of the P wave and the S wave

T.what: period of the S wave, read from the graph

A.what: amplitude of the S wave, read from the graph

parts.label: a
parts.examinerNote: Longitudinal against transverse, in terms of the direction of oscillation relative to the direction of energy transfer.

parts.label: b
parts.examinerNote: Both waves cover the same distance; the difference in travel times is the delay. A trial value (350 km gives 41 s) earns both marks if the arithmetic is shown.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.examinerNote: Read the period (two cycles in 2.5 s), then v = fλ. The answer is in km because the speed is in km/s.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.examinerNote: Up from equilibrium to the top, down to the bottom, back to equilibrium: four amplitudes. A distance moved by the medium, not by the wave.
